_comment: WHO OWNS WHICH AGENT — hand-maintained. Edit this file directly.
The data is at the TOP on purpose. It used to sit under twenty lines of prose, which made
the two assignments that matter easy to miss entirely when reading the file on GitHub.
THIS FILE CONTROLS PERMISSIONS. It is the source for .github/CODEOWNERS, which is
generated by scripts/gen_codeowners.py and checked in CI. Change an owner here and the
approval rights for that corpus follow. (It said the opposite until 2026-08-27 — 'no
effect on permissions' — which was true then and false the moment CODEOWNERS became
generated. Do not trust that sentence if you find it quoted anywhere else.)
It also drives the review UI (scripts/review_server.py), which highlights the transcripts
that are yours so you can find your rows without reading every line.
This is NOT contributors.json. That file is GENERATED from GitHub team membership and is
overwritten by scripts/sync_contributors.py — anything added there by hand is lost. This
file is the opposite: nothing generates it, so it is safe to edit and it is the only place
ownership is recorded.
default_owner  owns every corpus not named in by_agent, so adding an agent needs no change
here — it is owned by default until someone says otherwise.
by_agent       overrides, keyed by agent slug. The valid slugs are exactly the keys of
AGENT_FOLDER in scripts/gen_codeowners.py:
ops-center        -> Knowledge-OpsCenter
bp-general        -> Knowledge-BP-General
sac               -> Knowledge-SupportAccessCenter
identity          -> Knowledge-TylerIdentity
aligned-releases  -> Knowledge-AlignedReleases
status-page       -> Knowledge-StatusPageAndSLA
A value may be one username or a list of them.
Knowledge-Shared is deliberately absent and cannot be assigned here: its files upload to
ALL five collections, so a change there alters what every agent says. It stays admin-only.
'team' is NOT a corpus and must not appear in by_agent. A transcript answered by the team
router is owned by the admins — the review UI works that out from delegated_to, and the
router itself lives in team-config/, which is admin-only.
Names must match a `github` value in contributors.json, or the UI ignores them and says so
on the review page rather than silently highlighting nothing.
After editing: python3 scripts/gen_codeowners.py   (CI fails if you forget)
